clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old man with prior zygomatic implant placement six days earlier presented with acute painless swelling and crepitus around the left eye and cheek, with 2.5-mm relative proptosis. Physical exam confirmed subcutaneous emphysema. CT imaging revealed subcutaneous air in the left periocular area and orbit with a maxillary wall defect adjacent to the dental implant. Ophthalmologic exam showed preserved vision, normal pupils, intraocular pressure, and extraocular movements without optic nerve compromise. No signs of infection were present. The patient was observed without intervention, and the emphysema and proptosis resolved spontaneously over subsequent days.
